A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same NeuroMerging research despite the changed title. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original NeuroMerging evaluations on NLP, vision and Llama-2 benchmarks, alongside subspace and hyperparameter ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds baseline comparisons, cross-method subspace evaluations and computational resource measurements.

M1.justification: The masking, neuronal decomposition, SVD-based merging and scaling procedures remain unchanged. Algorithm 1 moves to Appendix A. The newly introduced input notation supports the activation derivation; v2 explicitly states that inputs are unnecessary during merging.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same seven T5 training/evaluation tasks, six held-out NLP datasets, eight vision datasets and CMMLU/GSM8K/HumanEval benchmarks. The new projection and efficiency analyses reuse existing dataset and task coverage.

E2.justification: v2 adds AdaMerging and AdaMerging++ to the vision comparisons in Table 4 and appendix Tables 13–14, specifying task-wise AdaMerging. AdaMerging was discussed but not evaluated in v1. The original comparator entries are retained.

E3.justification: The added experiments introduce orthogonal/parallel projection controls and runtime-in-seconds and memory-in-GB measurements (Appendices C.4–C.5). v2 also specifies the task-wise configuration for the added AdaMerging comparison. Existing model sizes, validation conditions, masking settings and hyperparameter searches remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendices C.4–C.5 substantially extend the diagnostic evidence: Tables 8–9 examine subspace projections across multiple merging methods and both NLP and vision models, while Tables 10–11 assess computational efficiency. The original merging-function, subspace-retention and hyperparameter ablations remain, with some relocated.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals or significance tests. The added results follow the existing point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: v2 adds substantive findings on projected-model performance and computational tradeoffs, plus AdaMerging scores. For example, Table 10 reports NeuroMerging at 161 seconds/69.1 GB versus TIES at 50 seconds/190.1 GB on T5-Large. Matched original benchmark values remain unchanged. AdaMerging++ on ViT-B/32 is inconsistently reported as 73.7 in Tables 4/13 and 73.1 in Table 11.

T1.justification: v2 adds activation-based derivations in Sections 3.1–3.3 and derives why orthogonal input components contribute nothing to pretrained neuronal activation in Appendix B, Equations 8–10. These provide limited mathematical support for the existing sensitivity/adaptability interpretation; the original decomposition and merging equations are retained.

C1.justification: Both versions claim a first neuronal perspective on merging, decomposition into sensitivity/adaptability subspaces, training-free NeuroMerging and superior NLP/vision performance. Reframing neuronal alignment as neuronal mechanisms and adding mathematical support do not materially change these central claims.

C2.justification: Appendix B adds an activation-based explanation for orthogonal merging, and C.4–C.5 interpret the new results as broader mechanistic and efficiency advantages. Some interpretations overreach: 'consistently enhances' overlooks TIES T5-Base declining from 76.4 to 76.2 under orthogonal projection, while efficiency claims understate runtime tradeoffs.

D1.justification: v2 adds a conditional code-release statement ('upon acceptance') and quantified merging resource costs. The hardware specification, checkpoint URLs, masking details and hyperparameter settings already appear in v1, although several are relocated. The code statement promises future availability rather than providing access.

R1.justification: Appendix C.5 adds references to work on TINT, Representation Surgery, EMR-Merging and Twin-Merging when positioning computational efficiency. The existing related-work taxonomy remains. Numerous other citation changes update metadata for the same works rather than introducing different research.

P1.justification: v2 retitles the paper, adds an author, revises the opening and concluding narrative, and recasts the methodological exposition around activation. It substantially reorganizes the appendices, relocating pseudocode, masking/checkpoint details and the merging-function ablation, and adds an Ethical Considerations section.

P2.justification: v2 adds an overview figure, a conceptual task-vector comparison table and four analysis tables, and expands vision tables with AdaMerging rows. All seven original figure images are retained, but substantial relocation/resizing, table-caption repositioning and movement of the taxonomy table and pseudocode reshape the presentation.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1, the activation derivations, additional baselines and cross-method/resource analyses make the neuronal rationale and practical tradeoffs easier to assess. The gain is limited: central results remain unchanged, while overstated projection/efficiency conclusions and the inconsistent AdaMerging++ score weaken the new reporting.
